cues.zh: 群体智慧，以 Hypermind 为例。
cues.en: Crowd wisdom, with Hypermind.

cues.zh: 本节课，你将了解一种集体智慧
cues.en: In this lesson, you will learn about one type of collective intelligence

cues.zh: 它出现在许多人共同猜测某件事的时候。简而言之，这个想法是
cues.en: that emerges when many people attempt to guess something. In a nutshell, the idea is that the

cues.zh: 众人汇总后的猜测，也就是群体的猜测，往往比个人的猜测准确得多。
cues.en: consolidated guess of many, the crowd’s guess, is often much more accurate than individual guesses.

cues.zh: 这一现象被称为“群体智慧”。群体预测正是利用了
cues.en: This phenomenon is known as “the wisdom of crowds”. Crowd forecasting simply leverages

cues.zh: 群体这种惊人的能力，对未来的集体猜测做出可靠的判断。
cues.en: this stunning ability of crowds to make reliable collective guesses about the future.

cues.zh: 我们将在接下来的课程中深入探讨预测，但首先，让我们了解一下群体智慧。
cues.en: We’ll go into forecasting in the next lessons, but first, let’s learn about the wisdom of crowds.

cues.zh: 群体智慧这一现象是在极端情况下被发现的
cues.en: The phenomenon of the wisdom of crowds was discovered in extremis

cues.zh: 1906年，由英国科学家 Francis Galton 发现，他是历史上最杰出的统计学家之一。
cues.en: in 1906 by the British scientist Francis Galton, one of the foremost statisticians of all time.

cues.zh: 我说“在极端情况下”，是因为高尔顿活到了84岁高龄！——
cues.en: I say “in extremis”, because Galton achieved the ripe old age of 84 years old! –

cues.zh: 而且在他发表这最后一项发现后仅仅几年就去世了。
cues.en: and died just a few years after publishing this last discovery.

cues.zh: 高尔顿在一个乡村集市上闲逛时，遇到了一群几百人
cues.en: Galton was visiting a country fair when he came across a crowd of several hundred people

cues.zh: 他们的注意力都集中在一头牛上。
cues.en: whose attention was focused on an ox.

cues.zh: 他们正在参加一场比赛，试图猜出这头牛的重量，或者更准确地说，
cues.en: They were participating in a contest to try to guess the weight of the animal, or to be precise,

cues.zh: 是猜出宰杀后能得到的肉的重量。
cues.en: to guess the weight of the meat that would come from butchering it.

cues.zh: 每位参与者支付少量入场费，并在票上写下自己最好的估计。
cues.en: Each participant paid a small entry fee and wrote their best estimate on a ticket.

cues.zh: 其中最准确的估计将赢得比赛，以及那份丰厚的肉奖品。
cues.en: The most accurate of these estimates would then win the contest, along with its meaty prize.

cues.zh: 高尔顿为什么会觉得这有趣呢？
cues.en: Why would Galton find this interesting?

cues.zh: 嗯，他意识到自己可以用这些估计来判断一大群非专业人士
cues.en: Well, he realized that he could use these estimates to find out whether a large number of non-specialists

cues.zh: 是否能做出明智的集体判断。当时，英国正在讨论
cues.en: could make a smart collective judgment. At the time, the United Kingdom was debating the idea

cues.zh: 一种更民主的政府形式，这使得群体智慧成为一个热门话题。
cues.en: of a more democratic form of government, making the wisdom of crowds a heated topic.

cues.zh: 作为王国精英的一员，
cues.en: As a member of the kingdom’s elite,

cues.zh: Galton 起初怀疑普通人能否做出准确判断。
cues.en: Galton was initially skeptical of the ability of laypeople to make accurate judgments.

cues.zh: 为了调查此事，Galton 安排比赛结束后收回所有票据。
cues.en: To investigate the matter, Galton arranged to retrieve all the tickets after the contest.

cues.zh: 他把 787 个估计值按升序排列，从最低的约 400 公斤到最高的约 700 公斤。
cues.en: He arranged the 787 estimates in ascending order from the lowest, at around 400 kg, to the highest, at around 700 kg.

cues.zh: 然后他找出最中间的那个估计值，称为中位数。
cues.en: He then identified the middle-most estimate, called the median.

cues.zh: 中位数非常特殊，
cues.en: The median is very special

cues.zh: 因为它是唯一一个不被大多数参与者认为过高或过低的估计值，
cues.en: because it is the only estimate that isn’t considered as too low or too high by a majority of the participants,

cues.zh: 也就是说，中位数之上和中位数之下的估计值数量完全相同。
cues.en: meaning there are exactly the same number of estimates above as there are below the median.

cues.zh: 这让 Galton 宣布中位数是 vox populi，即人民之声的衡量标准。换
cues.en: This brought Galton to declare the median to be a measure of the vox populi, the people’s voice. In

cues.zh: 句话说，就是整个群体的选择。这个中位数估计，即群体的估计，
cues.en: other words, the choice of the crowd as a whole. This median estimate, the crowd’s estimate,

cues.zh: 是 548 公斤，与实际牛的重量 543 公斤仅差 5 公斤。
cues.en: was 548 kg, just 5kg away from the actual ox’s weight of 543 kg.

cues.zh: 高尔顿随后计算了这些估计值的平均值——这是汇总群体猜测的另一种方式——
cues.en: Galton later computed the average of the estimates – another way to consolidate the crowd’s guess –

cues.zh: 结果竟然更准确，与实际重量仅差半公斤。
cues.en: and it turned out to be even more accurate, a mere half a kg away from the actual weight.

cues.zh: 群体智慧的三大原则 群体智慧遵循三条定律，高尔顿的
cues.en: The 3 principles of crowd wisdom The wisdom of crowds obeys 3 laws, which Galton’s

cues.zh: 例子完美地说明了这一点。第一条是，集体判断通常比大多数
cues.en: example illustrates perfectly. The first is that collective judgment is generally smarter than most

cues.zh: 个人判断更明智。我们可以通过比较群体中个体的平均误差
cues.en: individual judgments. We can test this claim by comparing the average error of an individual

cues.zh: 与整个群体平均值的误差来验证这一说法。在这个具体案例中，平均
cues.en: within the crowd, to the error of the full crowd average. In this particular case, the average

cues.zh: 个体误差——也就是随机挑一个人预期会有多大误差——约为4.5%，
cues.en: individual error – that is, how much error you’d expect picking someone at random – was about 4.5%,

cues.zh: 而整个群体的误差基本为0%。所以这完全吻合，引出
cues.en: while the error of the crowd as a whole was essentially 0%. So this checks out nicely, leading

cues.zh: 我们群体智慧的第一定律：“平均值的误差小于误差的平均值。”
cues.en: us to the first law of crowd wisdom : «the error of the average is smaller than the average error.»

cues.zh: 第二定律是群体规模很重要——群体越大越明智。看看随着我们把越来越多的
cues.en: The second law is that crowd size matters – larger crowds are smarter. Look at how the

cues.zh: 个体估计值纳入平均，群体的误差是如何减小的。
cues.en: error of the crowd diminishes as we include more and more individual estimates in the average.

cues.zh: 第三条法则体现在群体智慧曲线的形状上。它呈现出收益递减。
cues.en: The third law is visible in the shape of the crowd-wisdom curve. It exhibits diminishing

cues.zh: 随着群体规模扩大，误差起初急剧下降，之后下降得越来越慢。
cues.en: returns. As you increase the size of the crowd, the error falls sharply at first, and then more

cues.zh: 一个10人小组的误差比个人平均水平小3倍。
cues.en: and more slowly. A group of 10 has an error that is 3 times smaller than the average individual’s.

cues.zh: 但要把误差再缩小到三分之一，需要100人。而要再缩小到三分之一，则需要450人的群体……这意味着
cues.en: But it takes 100 people to divide the error by 3 again. And then a crowd of 450... The implication

cues.zh: 大部分集体智慧收益在初期就已获得：即便是小群体
cues.en: is that most of the collective-intelligence benefit is obtained at the start: even small

cues.zh: 也比个人聪明得多，你不需要庞大的群体就能变得明智很多。
cues.en: crowds are a lot smarter than individuals, and you don’t need a huge crowd to be a lot wiser.

cues.zh: 群体智慧背后的数学 好了，到目前为止我们描述了
cues.en: The maths behind crowd wisdom Ok, so far we have described

cues.zh: 群体智慧现象，但还没有真正解释它是如何运作的。
cues.en: the wisdom of crowds phenomenon, but we haven’t truly explained how it works.

cues.zh: 究竟有什么魔法能让一个聪明的集体判断从众多有缺陷的
cues.en: By what magic can a smart collective judgment emerge from the combination of many flawed

cues.zh: 个体判断中涌现出来？当然，这不是魔法……而是数学。核心观点
cues.en: individual judgments? Of course, it’s not magic... it’s mathematics. The central idea

cues.zh: 是每个人的判断都同时包含信息和误差。在许多情况下，
cues.en: is that everyone’s judgment contains both information and error. In many cases,

cues.zh: 每个判断都以不同的方式存在缺陷。所以当它们被组合起来时，信息会累加，
cues.en: every judgment is flawed in a different way. So when they are combined, information adds up,

cues.zh: 而误差则相互抵消。例如，在Galton的牛这个案例中，
cues.en: while errors cancel each other out. For example, in the case of Galton’s ox,

cues.zh: 有人可能把牛的重量低估了50公斤，而另一个人可能高估了
cues.en: someone may have underestimated its weight by 50 kg, while someone else could have overestimated

cues.zh: 47公斤。当这两个有误差的判断通过取平均组合起来时，
cues.en: it by 47 kg. When the two erroneous judgments are combined through averaging,

cues.zh: 结果只比真实体重少 1.5 公斤。判断几乎完全准确。
cues.en: the result is just 1.5 kg below the real weight. An almost perfectly accurate judgment.

cues.zh: 多样性定理 支撑群体智慧的数学公式
cues.en: The diversity theorem The mathematical formula that powers the wisdom of

cues.zh: 被称为“多样性定理”。它由美国社会学家 Scott Page 发现。
cues.en: crowds is called “the Diversity Theorem”. It was discovered by the American sociologist Scott Page.

cues.zh: 它看起来很复杂，但说的道理非常简单，却又深刻：集体误差等于
cues.en: It looks complicated, but what it says is very simple, yet profound: collective error equals

cues.zh: 个体误差的平均值，减去估计的多样性。换句话说，一个
cues.en: average individual error, minus the diversity of the estimates. In other words, the size of a

cues.zh: 群体的错误大小，在个体误差更小时会减小——这很明显——但它也会在
cues.en: groups’ mistake is reduced when individual errors are smaller – that’s obvious – but it is also

cues.zh: 不同的人犯不同的错误时减小。这就是多样性成分。
cues.en: reduced when different people make different mistakes. That’s the diversity component.

cues.zh: 因为这里有个减号，人们的分歧越大，群体就越聪明。这
cues.en: Because of the minus sign here, the more people disagree, the smarter the group becomes. That’s

cues.zh: 就是为什么观点的多样性——意味着误差的多样性能够相互
cues.en: why a diversity of opinions, which implies a diversity of errors that can cancel each other

cues.zh: 抵消——对集体智慧如此重要。所以你可以把这个公式简单理解为：
cues.en: out, is so important to collective intelligence. So you can read this formula as simply that a

cues.zh: 一个群体的集体智慧，既取决于个体的专业能力，也取决于多样的观点。
cues.en: group’s collective intelligence depends as much on individual expertise as on diverse opinions.

cues.zh: 专业知识和多样性是互补且可互换的。如果大多数人不是专家，
cues.en: Expertise and diversity are complementary and interchangeable. If most people aren’t experts,

cues.zh: 你可以通过寻求更高多样性的意见来弥补。
cues.en: you can compensate by seeking a higher diversity of opinions.

cues.zh: 或者如果每个人都想法一致，那他们最好得非常博学。
cues.en: Or if everyone thinks alike, then they’ better be very knowledgeable.

cues.zh: 专家与业余者 这里有一个实验的例子，
cues.en: Expert vs Amateurs Here’s an example from an experiment that

cues.zh: 是2011年由一群美国和以色列研究人员进行的。它考察了人们
cues.en: was run back in 2011 by a group of American and Israeli researchers. It looked at people’s ability

cues.zh: 预测美国审判结果的能力，具体来说是陪审团裁定的赔偿金额。
cues.en: to predict the results of trials in the United States, specifically the size of jury awards.

cues.zh: 有些参与者是拥有20年专业经验的资深律师，
cues.en: Some participants were experienced attorneys with 20 years of professional experience,

cues.zh: 而其他人是斯坦福大学法学院的学生，无疑非常聪明，但并没有
cues.en: while others were students at Stanford University Law School, very bright no doubt, but with no

cues.zh: 特别的专业知识。如你所见，学生的平均错误是
cues.en: particular expertise. As you can see, the average mistake of a student was twice as large as the

cues.zh: 律师平均错误的两倍。专业知识带来巨大差异！然而，当
cues.en: average mistake of an attorney. Expertise makes a huge difference! Yet, when the estimates of

cues.zh: 几个学生的估计被结合起来时，群体中意见的多样性弥补了
cues.en: several students are combined, the diversity of opinions in the group makes up for what

cues.zh: 它在个人专业知识上的不足。学生们的集体错误减少了，以至于14人
cues.en: it lacks in individual expertise. The students’ collective error diminishes so that a group of 14

cues.zh: 组成的小组和专家一样聪明。而15个学生组成的小组还稍微更聪明一些……
cues.en: is just as smart as an expert. And a group of 15 students is slightly smarter still...

cues.zh: 但专家之间也会有分歧，而且经常如此，所以他们的意见也可以结合起来，以
cues.en: But experts can also disagree, and they often do, so their opinions can also be combined for

cues.zh: 获得更准确的判断。仅结合2位专家的意见，就能将准确率提高25%。
cues.en: more accurate judgments. Combining just 2 expert opinions increases accuracy by 25%.

cues.zh: 而现在需要42名学生才能匹敌两位律师的表现。
cues.en: And now it takes 42 students to match the performance of two attorneys.

cues.zh: 遗憾的是，经验丰富的律师并不擅长采纳建议：他们对
cues.en: Sadly, experienced attorneys are bad at taking advice : they give less weight to

cues.zh: 同行的估计重视不足，因此无法收获群体智慧的好处。
cues.en: their peer’s estimates and therefore fail to reap the benefits of the crowd’s wisdom.

cues.zh: 集体智慧的配方 说了这么多关于明智群体的讨论，
cues.en: The collective intelligence recipe All this talk about wise crowds is all

cues.zh: 听起来都不错，但我们不都遇到过极其愚蠢的群体吗？我们每个人
cues.en: well and good, but haven’t we all encountered deeply stupid groups? Has each and every one

cues.zh: 不都亲眼见证过，即使是聪明人——也许甚至是我们自己——也会在
cues.en: of us not personally witnessed that even smart people – perhaps even ourselves – can become

cues.zh: 融入群体后变得愚蠢吗？当然，集体愚蠢也同样存在。
cues.en: stupid when they become part of a crowd? Of course, collective stupidity also exists.

cues.zh: 有聪明的群体，也有愚蠢的群体，而大多数群体确实天生就是愚蠢的。
cues.en: There are smart crowds and stupid crowds, and most crowds are indeed naturally stupid.

cues.zh: 要让群体变聪明，就需要合理地组织它。集体智慧的配方，
cues.en: To make a crowd smart, you need to organize it properly. The recipe for collective intelligence,

cues.zh: 改编自美国记者James Surowiecki的著名著作，告诉我们该怎么做：
cues.en: adapted from the famous book by American journalist James Surowiecki, tells us how:

cues.zh: 首先，必须激励每个人去思考，并且独立地思考。独立性
cues.en: First of all, everyone must be incentivized to think, and to do so independently. Independence

cues.zh: 能让多样化的观点蓬勃发展，因为它允许并鼓励个体表达
cues.en: allows for a diversity of opinions to flourish, by allowing and encouraging individuals to express

cues.zh: 自己独特的视角。智慧的大敌是从众，而不是群体
cues.en: their unique perspectives. The enemy of intelligence is conformity, not the crowd

cues.zh: 本身。一个聪明的群体应当设法让所有分歧意见都浮现出来，而不是寻求共识。
cues.en: itself. A smart group should seek to surface all diverging opinions instead of seeking consensus.

cues.zh: 然后，最后一步确保群体即便存在分歧也能做出决策：
cues.en: Then, a final step ensures the group can make decisions despite the disagreements:

cues.zh: 客观聚合。最合适的聚合机制
cues.en: objective aggregation. The most relevant aggregation mechanism

cues.zh: 取决于特定群体想要做什么。如果任务是选出一位领导者，
cues.en: depends on what a given crowd is trying to do. If it is tasked with choosing a leader,

cues.zh: 多数投票就是个好办法。如果任务是猜一头牛的重量，
cues.en: a majority vote is a good solution. If it is asked to guess the weight of an ox,

cues.zh: 对所有估计值取数学平均就可以了。如果任务是预测未来，
cues.en: a mathematical average of all estimates will do fine. If it is trying to predict the future,

cues.zh: 让人们就结果下注，就是整合分歧预测的有力方式。
cues.en: letting people place bets on outcomes is a powerful way to consolidate divergent forecasts.

cues.zh: 本质上，这就是群体预测的核心：用群体智慧预测未来。
cues.en: In essence, this is what crowd forecasting is about: using crowd wisdom to predict the future.
